text:
lee: Heads-up — OSS vuln scan flagged three entries impacting our Go service surfaces: CVE-2026-XXXXX (net/http / Go runtime), CVE-2026-YYYY (github.com/golang-jwt/jwt), CVE-2026-ZZZZ (google.golang.org/grpc). Can we triage quickly?

dep-bot: automated-scan: Found vulnerable modules in repo 'inference-runtime':
- google.golang.org/grpc v1.54.0 -> fixed in v1.56.0
- github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4 v4.4.0 -> fixed in v4.4.3
- Go stdlib net/http issue fixed in go1.21.5
Links: https://oss-scan.example/cves/1752

miguel: Quick impact check: our go.mod pins grpc v1.54.0 and jwt v4.4.0. We build on go1.21.3 so net/http vuln applies. Prioritization: grpc=High (streaming endpoints), net/http=High (runtime), jwt=Medium (edgecase token validation). Recommend urgent hotfix for grpc+jwt and runtime upgrade to 1.21.5.

sara: +1. grpc risk looks exploitable in our long-lived streaming inference channels. jwt vuln seems to affect some validation paths when alg header is manipulated, lower probability but real.

lee: Ops, can you run a canary with updated grpc+jwt on staging and bump runtime to 1.21.5? Need audit logs to confirm no auth regressions. @ops-oncall

ops-oncall: I can take this. Plan: 
1) branch: patch/grpc-jwt-pins
2) run: `go get google.golang.org/grpc@v1.56.0 github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v4@v4.4.3` and update go.mod/go.sum
3) deploy canary with go1.21.5 runtime image to staging nodes
4) run smoke tests + replay recent auth traffic against staging to look for anomalies
Estimated: canary by EOD.

miguel: Add a module pin comment in go.mod referencing CVE and enforce in CI: fail if grpc < v1.56.0 or jwt < v4.4.3. Also add a backport note for Dedicated customers running older releases.

sara: I'll run E2E KMS signing/verification with the new jwt lib on staging keys — possible signing edgecases. Will also run token replay against canary service.

lee: Who will open the PR and own the rollout?

miguel: I'll open PR. Will include:
- go.mod/go.sum bumps
- short changelog entry referencing CVE IDs
- CI gating job snippet: `exit 1 if go list -m all | grep -E "google.golang.org/grpc@(0|[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)"` (will tighten)
- rollback instructions

dep-bot: created issue #842: vuln-triage-go-deps (assigned to miguel)

ops-oncall: Canary timeline: deploy staging by EOD, monitor 24h, if clean start gradual prod rollout with 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 6h windows. Rollback if error budget spike > 2x baseline.

sara: QA checklist for PR: 
- KMS sign/verify E2E
- auth regression smoke (token issuance + refresh)
- perf smoke for grpc streaming (latency + memory)
- log grep for "token invalid" and "grpc: connection" errors

lee: Good. Label as high-priority vuln-triage; unless we see active exploit, keep incident channel as vuln-triage. Update here with PR and telemetry.

miguel: PR WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/1298 — includes module bumps and CI check. Please review.

sara: I'll run KMS e2e once PR merged to staging. Also adding a small test that signs with KMS-backed key and verifies with jwt lib to catch any alg differences.

ops-oncall: Rollback plan: pin modules back to previous versions and redeploy previous runtime image. Keep canary up for at least 1 hour before wider rollout.

miguel: Reminder for release notes: explicitly mention CVE IDs, fixed versions: grpc@v1.56.0, jwt@v4.4.3, go1.21.5 runtime.

dep-bot: vulnerability status updated: in-progress -> monitoring.

lee: Thanks everyone. Keep updates in this thread: post canary deploy ts and any anomalous telemetry. If we see exploit indicators, we'll escalate to incidents.

ops-oncall: Canary deployed at 2026-03-20T18:12Z to staging-01. Monitoring dashboards live.

miguel: PR merged to staging at 2026-03-20T19:05Z. Running full canary smoke suite now.

sara: KMS e2e passed on staging. No token failures seen in 45m.

lee: Closing loop for now. Move to monitoring and schedule prod rollout tomorrow morning per ops plan if no regressions.
